comment: Hostile corpus for SBFBPromptAgentPack.v1 (Sprint 83 Phase F). Every entry carries the RAW envelope bytes a caller could hand to verify_signed_pack, plus the error variant that MUST come back; entries sharing a variant also pin WHICH rule fired via expect_detail_contains. Enumerating the corpus in a committed file is what makes '100% refused' a measurable claim instead of a slogan: the test iterates this file, and an entry whose refusal changes shape fails loudly. Entries here are refused BEFORE the signature is even considered — their 'signature' fields are deliberately junk, so any entry that reached Ed25519 verification would surface as SignatureInvalid and fail its expectation. Post-signature refusals (valid signature over an unacceptable body) cannot live in a static file — they need a real signing key — and are built in code in the same module (valid_signature_over_hostile_body_is_terminal), which asserts BY NAME that every post_signature_entries row below is exercised. The one exception is cross-domain-signature, exercised in tests::cross_domain_signature_rejected because it needs the domain-injectable door. SVG/Markdown/script content classes are absent BY CONSTRUCTION of the v1 root: the pack embeds no file content at all (PACK.lock carries path+digest+size only), so there is nothing to sanitise at this layer; the content-level hostile surface belongs to whatever materialises the pinned files. The TypeScript parity mirror lives at web/src/workflow/__tests__/pack_digest.test.ts.

entries.name: not-json
entries.why: raw bytes that are not JSON at all

entries.name: envelope-is-array
entries.why: top level must be an object, not an array

entries.name: envelope-extra-member
entries.why: an unknown envelope member could smuggle a second interpretation

entries.name: envelope-no-signature
entries.why: an unsigned envelope must never be treated as a draft to render

entries.name: envelope-signature-not-string
entries.why: signature must be a hex string, not a structure

entries.name: duplicate-key-in-envelope
entries.why: serde_json keeps the last duplicate; a first-wins parser elsewhere reads a different envelope out of the same bytes

entries.name: duplicate-key-in-payload
entries.why: same cross-parser differential, one level down — the signed name would depend on which parser you ask

entries.name: payload-null-member
entries.why: null is not canonically representable (nested non-finite floats collapse to it; absent-vs-null is a consumer ambiguity)

entries.name: payload-null-nested-in-array
entries.why: the null rejection must reach inside arrays, not only top-level members

entries.name: integer-beyond-2-53
entries.why: beyond IEEE-754 exact range a TypeScript verifier reads a different number back

entries.name: oversized-array
entries.why: cardinality bomb: a huge array of cheap values

entries.name: oversized-string
entries.why: a single string larger than the string cap

entries.name: deep-nesting
entries.why: depth bomb: recursion beyond the depth cap

entries.name: oversized-envelope
entries.why: an envelope past the byte cap dies on the size bound (checked on the raw slice before any parse; the corpus can only observe the resulting TooLarge, not instrument serde)

entries.name: lone-surrogate-escape
entries.why: a lone UTF-16 surrogate escape has no scalar value; JSON text carrying one must die at the parser, never reach canonicalisation (generated: the corpus file itself must stay parseable)

post_signature_entries.name: valid-signature-over-unknown-field
post_signature_entries.why: the cosign failure mode: a genuine signature over a body that fails the typed parse must be a TERMINAL refusal, never a degraded 'verified' status

post_signature_entries.name: valid-signature-over-wrong-format-version
post_signature_entries.why: a signature does not make a future format version acceptable

post_signature_entries.name: valid-signature-over-zip-slip-path
post_signature_entries.why: path traversal in PACK.lock, refused by shape since this crate cannot resolve paths

post_signature_entries.name: valid-signature-over-backslash-path
post_signature_entries.why: Windows separator refused outright rather than normalised

post_signature_entries.name: valid-signature-over-absolute-path
post_signature_entries.why: an absolute path escapes the pack root at materialisation time

post_signature_entries.name: valid-signature-over-drive-letter-path
post_signature_entries.why: a drive or NTFS stream separator escapes the pack root

post_signature_entries.name: valid-signature-over-reserved-device-name
post_signature_entries.why: all 22 DOS device names resolve to devices on Windows regardless of directory

post_signature_entries.name: valid-signature-over-duplicate-lock-path
post_signature_entries.why: two entries for one path make the content digest ambiguous

post_signature_entries.name: valid-signature-over-case-colliding-paths
post_signature_entries.why: paths differing only by case are one file on Windows/macOS filesystems

post_signature_entries.name: valid-signature-over-trailing-dot-segment
post_signature_entries.why: Win32 strips trailing dots: two spellings, one file

post_signature_entries.name: valid-signature-over-confusable-path
post_signature_entries.why: Unicode confusables fall outside the ASCII-only v1 lock-path alphabet

post_signature_entries.name: valid-signature-over-unsorted-lock
post_signature_entries.why: one file set must have one canonical entry order; a producer free to reorder would mint several content digests for one pack

post_signature_entries.name: valid-signature-over-oversized-file
post_signature_entries.why: a declared size beyond the per-file cap promises a materialiser more than the format admits

post_signature_entries.name: valid-signature-over-empty-lock
post_signature_entries.why: a lock that pins no file attests to nothing

post_signature_entries.name: valid-signature-over-mismatched-content-digest
post_signature_entries.why: the content digest is recomputed from the lock, never taken at its word

post_signature_entries.name: valid-signature-over-duplicate-subject-name
post_signature_entries.why: duplicate subject names make provenance ambiguous

post_signature_entries.name: valid-signature-over-empty-subject-list
post_signature_entries.why: provenance with no subject attests to nothing

post_signature_entries.name: valid-signature-over-materialised-secret
post_signature_entries.why: secret_refs must stay opaque logical references; a pasted credential is refused by the format itself

post_signature_entries.name: valid-signature-over-truncated-digest
post_signature_entries.why: a digest that is not 64 lowercase hex chars cannot pin anything (mutates graph_semantic so the content-binding rule cannot mask the syntax rule)

post_signature_entries.name: valid-signature-over-uppercase-digest
post_signature_entries.why: hex has two spellings per digest; the format admits exactly one (mutates graph_semantic, same masking discipline)

post_signature_entries.name: cross-domain-signature
post_signature_entries.why: a signature minted under another SBFB domain must not verify as a pack
